title: TUESDAY UPPER PUSH AND POSTURE
subtitle: GENTLE ARMS, TALL POSTURE. ALL SEATED FIRST, THEN STANDING AT THE WALL AND CHAIR. NO FLOOR TODAY. KIND HIPS.

script.welcome: Good morning Pam. I'm Stratton. Tuesday is upper push and posture, about eleven minutes, nice and easy. In the chair we'll do gentle rows, a light overhead press, and a soft figure four. Then we stand for wall push ups, a kind hip flexor stretch, and a little balance at the chair. No floor today. Hand weights are optional, and a smaller range is fine on sore-joint days. Lovely to see you.
script.start: Whenever you're ready. Sit tall near the front of a sturdy chair, feet flat, shoulders soft and down, and take one slow easy breath.
script.nextExercise: Next one. Settle in. No rush at all.
script.lastSet: Last one of these. Keep it comfortable.
script.complete: That's us, Pam. Shoulders open, posture tall, hips looked after. Another small win in the book. Have a sip of water and enjoy your Tuesday. Well done.
script.pause: Paused. Take all the time you need.
script.resume: Back with you. Easy as we go.

exercises.name: SEATED ROW (LIGHT OR NO WEIGHTS)
exercises.cue: Sit tall near the front of the chair, feet flat. Hold light hand weights or nothing at all, arms reaching forward at chest height. Draw the elbows back close to your sides, gently squeeze the shoulder blades together, then reach forward again slowly. Keep the shoulders down away from the ears. A smaller pull is fine on sore-joint days.
exercises.speakStart: Seated rows to wake up the upper back. Eight slow ones, twice through. Reach forward, then draw the elbows back and gently squeeze the shoulder blades. Weights are optional.
exercises.speakRest: Twenty seconds. Hands in your lap. Slow breath.
exercises.speakDone: Rows done. Lovely tall back, Pam.

exercises.name: SEATED OVERHEAD PRESS (GENTLE)
exercises.cue: Sit tall, tummy gently in. Start with hands at shoulder height, palms forward, with very light weights or empty hands. Press slowly up only as high as feels comfortable, then lower with control. No need to lock the elbows or go all the way overhead. If a shoulder grumbles, press lower or skip the weights.
exercises.speakStart: Gentle overhead press. Six slow ones, twice through. Hands at the shoulders, press up only as high as feels comfortable, then lower slowly. Empty hands are perfectly fine.
exercises.speakRest: Twenty seconds. Arms down. Roll the shoulders gently.

exercises.name: SEATED FIGURE-FOUR (LIGHT)
exercises.cue: Sit tall near the front of the chair, feet flat. Rest the right ankle over the left thigh, just above the knee. Stay tall and tip forward from the hips only a touch, until you feel a mild stretch in the outer hip. Hold about twenty seconds, then switch sides. Never press the knee down or fold deep. If the left groin or front of the hip pinches, skip that side or simply rest the ankle without leaning. Stop if you feel sharp groin pain, spreading pain, numbness, tingling, or weakness.
exercises.speakStart: Seated figure four, nice and light. About twenty seconds each side. Rest one ankle over the other thigh, sit tall, and tip forward just a touch. Skip the left side if it pinches.
exercises.speakRest: Fifteen seconds. Both feet down. Then we stand up and come to the wall.
exercises.speakDone: Figure four done. Take your time standing up, and come to the wall.

exercises.name: WALL PUSH-UPS
exercises.cue: Stand an arm's length from the wall, hands flat at shoulder height and a little wider than the shoulders. Keep the body in one long line and bend the elbows to bring your chest gently toward the wall, then press back. Stand closer to make it easier. Keep the wrists comfortable, and on sore-joint days only bend a little.
exercises.speakStart: Wall push ups. Six slow ones, twice through. Hands on the wall at shoulder height, bend the elbows, chest toward the wall, and press away. Step closer to make it easier.
exercises.speakRest: Twenty five seconds. Shake out the hands. Easy breath.
exercises.speakDone: Wall push ups done. That's real strength, Pam. Come over to the chair.

exercises.name: STANDING HIP FLEXOR
exercises.cue: Stand beside the chair with one hand lightly on the chair back. Step one foot back about half a step, not a deep lunge, both feet pointing forward, knees soft. Gently tuck the pelvis under until you feel a mild stretch at the front of the back hip. A tiny lean is enough. Breathe slowly for about twenty seconds, then swap. Start with the left leg back and keep that side extra gentle. Stop if you feel sharp groin pain, spreading pain, numbness, tingling, or weakness.
exercises.speakStart: Standing hip flexor. About twenty seconds each leg. Hand on the chair, small step back, tuck the pelvis, tiny lean. Left leg first, extra gentle.
exercises.speakRest: Fifteen seconds. Feet together. Easy breath.
exercises.speakDone: Hip flexor stretch done. Front of the hips looked after.

exercises.name: CHAIR-SUPPORTED BALANCE
exercises.cue: Stand tall behind the chair with both hands resting lightly on the back. Shift your weight onto one foot and lift the other heel, or the whole foot, just off the floor. Keep the standing knee soft, shoulders back and down, eyes ahead. Hold about fifteen seconds, then switch. Grip the chair as much as you need; toes touching down is perfectly fine. Keep the lifted leg low and relaxed so nothing pinches at the front of the hip.
exercises.speakStart: Chair balance to finish. About fifteen seconds each leg, twice through. Hands on the chair, stand tall, shoulders back, and lift one foot just off the floor. Toes can touch down any time.
exercises.speakDone: Balance done. That's the session, Pam. Posture tall and arms awake. Have a lovely Tuesday.
